SysArch-02 reviewed **`f8967e9b6f86b807b088d187cf2acc6e50e63ce1`**. No files changed.

The service implementation matches my independent calculations:

- Baseline: **516.155 L power envelope**, **37.254 L fibre envelope**, **56 cooling trunk pairs/end**.
- Reaggregation savings: **242.734 L** for 1/2 barrel/endcap bundles per network; **273.421 L** for 1/1.
- One-end service areas: **128,902.563 → 78,133.169 / 67,979.290 mm²**.
- Worst-sector equivalent widths: **75.590 → 46.717 / 41.000 mm**.
- Fixed HV leakage remains outside LV rail current. Board load, fibres, cooling and trays remain fixed.
- Gross envelope volumes, conductor-only sensitivity and hardware qualifications are appropriately distinguished.

Actual checks: **5/5 service tests passed**, plus independent assertions covering baseline values and **all 24 cases** for volumes, final cross-section and worst-sector widths.

One small completion gap: `DES-042:84–85` promises separate material litres, but `services.py:155` reports only the distinct conductor-resizing upper proxy. Add recipe-derived removed constituents for the bundle-removal hypothesis:

| Bundle state | Copper | Polyimide | Internal void |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 2 | 48.547 L | 72.820 L | 121.367 L |
| 1 / 1 | 54.684 L | 82.026 L | 136.711 L |

These use the existing **20% Cu / 30% PI / 50% air effective recipe**; they do not qualify electrical gauges. Keep them distinct from `upper_LV_copper_material_saved_L`.

Also retain the baseline limitation: its worst-sector **75.590 mm** equivalent demand already exceeds the existing **73 mm** corridor before walls and bend allowances. No geometric or engineering acceptance follows from the calculation.
